note: Adversarial review findings (item-quality and compliance lenses) from the 15-17 Oct review round, recovered from the workflow transcripts after the device move. Not yet acted on. The compliance lens was added on 18 Oct 2026 (review on the new device).

item-quality.verdict: Refuted as currently built. The instruction is clear and self-contained, every number the oracle uses is stated, the start graph fails correctly (f2p false, p2p true), and the parameter-tune family and L1 level are defensible. But the purity oracle wrongly rejects answers that meet the stated requirement. oracles.band_fraction counts DC power twice on real signals. ./gb ladder rejects a 2.4/3.6 kHz Hamming band-pass with 950 Hz transitions (true 31.2 dB) and a 2.425/3.575 kHz one (true 32.4 dB), though both clear the stated 30 dB. The author's borderline example (2.4/3.6 kHz, 1 kHz width) truly reaches 30.02 dB, so it passes the stated spec, contrary to the note. Even after the oracle fix, the 30 dB threshold sits on the most natural minimal retune and should be moved to give a margin. Smaller issues: this item is a template twin of the test item gbf-test-12, the 'keep blocks/connections' constraint is never checked, and the 'fifth harmonic' sentence gives away the key step. Scratch evidence: ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-05/ (alt05_*.grc, probe05*.py).

findings.claim: The V6 purity check rejects answers that meet the stated requirement (3). oracles.band_fraction sums |rfft|^2 for real signals without doubling the non-DC bins, so it actually computes P_band / (P_total + P_DC). The DC power is counted twice. The instruction defines purity as a share of 'the power' and explicitly puts 'its DC level' in the 30 dB budget. This clock has a strong DC component (0.5, about 15 dB above the 5th harmonic), so DC leakage is a large part of the residual. As a result, valid designs are rejected. The authoring note that the 2.4/3.6 kHz, 1 kHz-transition design is '29.3 dB, 0.7 dB short, correct under the stated spec' is wrong: under the stated spec that design passes.
findings.evidence: I ran ./gb ladder with items/tier_f/dev/gbf-dev-05/task.json on three variants of the start graph in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-05/. Each sets clock 600 Hz, level 1.178*5/3 and default Hamming window, and changes only the BPF cutoffs and transition width. All three fail at V6, with only the band_fraction check failing (f2p true, p2p false): (a) 2400/3600 Hz, width 1000: oracle 0.998833; true one-sided power fraction 0.999006 (30.02 dB, meets the spec). (b) 2400/3600 Hz, width 950: oracle 0.998761 (29.1 dB); true 0.999233 (31.2 dB). (c) 2425/3575 Hz, width 950: oracle 0.998964; true 0.999427 (32.4 dB, a 2.4 dB margin). I checked the true fraction with Parseval: the time-domain mean power 0.0316864 equals the one-sided doubled spectral sum, while the oracle's denominator is 0.0158459, i.e. half the power plus the DC power again. The residual of design (a) is DC -37.6 dB, 1.8 kHz -31.5 dB and 4.2 kHz -39.2 dB relative to the tone. In a 221-design grid (Hamming, symmetric cutoffs ±500-800 Hz, widths 500-1300 Hz), 5 designs pass the stated spec but are rejected by the oracle (scratch probe probe05c.py).
findings.suggested_fix: Fix oracles.band_fraction for real input so it measures power: weight bins 1..N/2-1 by 2 (DC and, for even N, Nyquist by 1), or use the two-sided FFT and select |f| in [lo, hi]. Then rerun the gates for every task that uses band_fraction on real signals with DC or Nyquist content. For this task, I checked that after the fix the reference (99.998 %), v1, v2 and v3 (≥ 99.987 %) still pass, and every purity mutant is still killed (true fraction ≤ 0.9754). Correct the 'borderline_designs' note in task.json and the build.py docstring.

findings.claim: The 99.9 % / 30 dB purity threshold sits exactly on the most natural minimal retune. A developer who centres the passband midway between the 1.8, 3 and 4.2 kHz harmonics (2.4/3.6 kHz) and keeps the start graph's 1 kHz transition and Hamming window gets a true purity of 30.02 dB. That is 0.02 dB above the threshold under the correct metric and 0.7 dB below it under the current oracle. Whether this answer passes depends on a hair's breadth and on a GNU Radio detail the instruction gives no way to anticipate: firdes sizes a Hamming filter as 53*fs/(22*width), which gives 115 taps for a nominal 1 kHz width, but a 115-tap Hamming filter's real transition is about 1.4 kHz. The item's difficulty at this point measures sensitivity to that heuristic rather than design skill.
findings.evidence: Probe (probe05d.py, same GNU Radio blocks as the ladder; the oracle values match ./gb ladder exactly). Clear failures: clock-only retune 82.3 %, rectangular window 97.5 %, 2-4 kHz with 400 Hz width 99.465 %, 2.1/3.9 kHz with 600 Hz width 99.466 %, 2.4/3.6 kHz with 1200 Hz width 99.38 %, Hann 2.4/3.6 kHz with 1000 Hz width 99.01 %. Natural designs: 2.4/3.6 kHz with 1000 Hz width 99.9006 % (true), width 950 99.923 %, 2.5/3.5 kHz with 1000 Hz width 99.989 %, Hann 2.4/3.6 kHz with 600 Hz width 99.988 %. All purity mutants are ≤ 97.5 %, so no mutant needs a threshold as tight as 99.9 %.
findings.suggested_fix: After fixing F1, move the threshold so that natural designs have a margin on both sides, e.g. ≥ 99.7 % (about 25 dB). That leaves ≥ 2.4 dB to the probed bad designs (≤ 99.47 %) and about 4.8 dB to the minimal-retune design, and every mutant is still killed. Restate it in the instruction ('at least 99.7 % ... at least 25 dB below the tone') and in spec_properties. Alternatively, deliberately make the 1 kHz-width design fail with a clear margin (e.g. ≥ 99.95 % / 33 dB) and record that choice for the reviewers.

findings.claim: gbf-dev-05 is a template twin of the test item gbf-test-12, and close to test-07 and test-08. All are parameter-tune or repair L1 items built the same way: a square-wave clock from a Signal Source goes through an FIR filter and a Multiply Const (a π-multiple constant) into a File Sink; the clock frequency changes and the filter and level must be retuned to keep a clean tone. The measurement wording is the same ('steady-state output after the first 4096 samples', RMS within 5 %, '≥ 99.9x % of the power within ±100 Hz ... N dB below the tone'). The chain-signature rule is met only because the filter block id differs (band_pass vs low_pass), so the two items get different cluster_ids and count as independent clusters.
findings.evidence: items/tier_f/test/gbf-test-12/start.grc has clock_src (GR_SQR_WAVE) -> lpf -> level (0.7854) -> sine_sink, and its instruction says 'The clock is moving to 2 kHz. Tune the flowgraph ...'. gbf-dev-05's authoring_notes.related_items acknowledges the relationship. Eval plan §6 defines 'template twins such as the same flowgraph question for a different signal' as near-twins.
findings.suggested_fix: Either rebase this dev item on a different template (e.g. a non-clock source, or a different measured property), or record the dev-05/test-12 pair as twins so that dev-based decisions (prompt choice, checkpoint selection) are not reported as independent of that test template. Consider sharing a cluster id for the clustered standard errors.

findings.claim: The instruction requires 'make the change by retuning parameter values only: keep the existing blocks and their connections', but nothing checks it. An answer that adds a second filter, swaps the band-pass for a low-pass/high-pass pair, or adds blocks gets full credit. A parameter-tune item therefore cannot tell a retune apart from a redesign.
findings.evidence: task.json oracle.checks contains only V6 signal features. ladder.py and gates.py have no structural assertion. The author records this in authoring_notes.unchecked_scope_constraint.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add a structural check, e.g. a multiset comparison of the answer's block ids and connection topology against start.grc (partial_credit.py could supply it), scored as a separate flag or a V6 'main' check, or soften the sentence to a preference so that the instruction states no requirement the grader ignores.

findings.claim: The sentence 'so the multiplier has to work from the clock's fifth harmonic instead of its third' gives away the key reasoning step (3 kHz / 600 Hz = 5). That makes the remaining work largely mechanical: scale the gain by 5/3 and recentre the passband. A user would plausibly say it, but it lowers the parameter-tune difficulty beyond what the numeric target alone requires.
findings.evidence: task.json instruction, 4th sentence. The 3 kHz output target and the 600 Hz clock already determine the harmonic.
findings.suggested_fix: Optionally drop the clause, keeping 'My clock is changing to 600 Hz, but I still need the same 3 kHz output', so the model has to infer which harmonic to use. The team decides.

compliance.verdict: Mechanically compliant, but not fully compliant with the 16 Oct oracle policy. I re-ran ./gb tier-f gates; every gate passes (10/10 solvability, 276 tokens, 3/3 variants, start fails at V6 with f2p false and p2p true, 17/17 valid mutants killed). Running build.py twice in scratch reproduces task.json, start.grc, reference.grc and all variants byte for byte. The canary appears only in task.json (and the non-model-visible build.py). id, directory and split agree. The signature hashes to dev regardless of connection or stage order, so there was no shopping. Licence, source, cluster_id, provenance and review follow the set convention, and an original composed chain correctly has no perturbation. The disjointness claim holds against training_task_specs.json, and the contamination audit raises no flag. Each mutant is valid, is spec-breaking and is killed by the property its 'breaks' label names. The stated tolerances match the checks. Refuted on: C1, the parameter-only and 'keep their connections' scope cannot be checked with the existing graph-check kinds (same_blocks_as_start ignores connections, counts variables, and fails from the ./gb ladder CLI); C2, the 48 kHz sample rate and the 'square wave' are unchecked (a scaled 96 kHz answer and a level-matched triangle clock pass V6); C3, records stale after the band_fraction fix and reviewer alternatives missing from variants; C4, the 1 % clock latitude is illusory; C5, train-hashed functional twins. Near-duplication with gbf-test-12 is item-quality F3 and is not repeated. Scratch evidence: ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-05/compliance/.

findings.claim: The 16 Oct oracle policy needs a graph check for 'make the change by retuning parameter values only: keep the existing blocks and their connections'. Item-quality F4 already notes that nothing checks it. New point: the check kinds that exist cannot express it. same_blocks_as_start compares only the multiset of block ids, so an answer that rewires the blocks still passes. It also counts variable blocks, so an answer that adds one helper variable fails. Adding same_blocks_as_start, the obvious fix, would therefore leave 'their connections' unchecked and could reject an answer the instruction arguably allows.
findings.evidence: Scratch task ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-05/compliance/task_gc.json is task.json plus oracle.graph_checks [{kind: same_blocks_as_start, group: main}] and _dir. ./gb ladder results: (a) cx_rewired_level_first.grc (clock_src -> level -> bpf -> out_sink; the same blocks, connections changed) passes V1-V6 with the plain task.json and with task_gc.json ('same block types'; purity 0.999983, out RMS 0.17792). (b) cx_added_variable.grc (adds variable f_clk = 600 and sets freq f_clk, cutoffs 4*f_clk / 6*f_clk, width f_clk) passes every signal check, but with task_gc.json it fails V6 on same_blocks_as_start: "added {'variable': 1}". (c) reference.grc passes with task_gc.json. (d) The documented './gb ladder <grc> --task task.json' never sets task['_dir'], so same_blocks_as_start always fails with 'no start graph'. The reference with task_gc_nodir.json fails at V6 that way. Once the check is added, anyone reproducing a result with the CLI gets false rejections.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide this together with F4. Option (a): keep the sentence and check it fully. Add a connection check, e.g. a new kind 'same_connections_as_start' whose multiset of (source block id, port, sink block id, port) edges must equal the start graph's. Restrict same_blocks_as_start to functional blocks, or say 'do not add variables' in the instruction. Use group main. Option (b): reword the sentence as a preference, or drop 'and their connections'. In both cases, change ladder.main so that it sets task['_dir'] to the --task file's folder. Then re-run the gates.

findings.claim: Two more stated requirements are not checked, which the 16 Oct oracle policy does not allow. The first is 'Keep the 48 kHz sample rate'. The second is that clock_in.dat records 'a 600 Hz square wave'. The mean and RMS checks fix the levels of a square wave, but they do not check that the clock is a square wave. Neither requirement is listed in spec_properties.
findings.evidence: ./gb ladder with the task's task.json: ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-05/compliance/cx_samp_rate_96k_scaled.grc (samp_rate 96000, clock 1200 Hz, band-pass 4.8/7.2 kHz with width 1.2 kHz, level 1.9635) writes the same samples as the reference and passes V1-V6 (clock 600.0 Hz, purity 0.999983). cx_triangle_level_matched.grc (waveform GR_TRI_WAVE, amp 1.7320508, offset -0.3660254, giving mean 0.5 and RMS 0.707; level 8.904; the reference band-pass) also passes V1-V6: clock mean 0.5, clock RMS 0.707327, out RMS 0.1791, purity 0.999723. Yet its clock_in.dat holds a triangle that runs from -0.37 to 1.37. The authored waveform mutant (#6, triangle 0..1) is killed only because its RMS (0.577) is wrong; a triangle with matched levels survives.
findings.suggested_fix: Sample rate: add a graph check block_present {ids: [variable], params: {value: '48000'}}, which compares numerically and so accepts 48e3. Alternatively, reword so that both files are read as 48 kHz streams and the sample rate is no longer a separate requirement. Square wave: add a clock check that only a 0/1 square wave meets, e.g. corr_ref >= 0.995 against a few periods of the 600 Hz 0/1 square wave, with time shifts allowed. In a numpy check with oracles.corr_ref, an 8-period reference (max_lag 80) scores a shifted square 1.0 and the matched triangle 0.933. Add the level-matched triangle as a mutant. List both requirements in spec_properties.

findings.claim: After the 18 Oct band_fraction fix the item still passes every gate, but its own records are now wrong. Also, none of the alternatives the item-quality reviewer showed is among the variants, although the rules say to add one for each. Item-quality F1 already asks to correct the note; new here are the post-fix numbers and the missing variants.
findings.evidence: I re-ran ./gb tier-f gates at 2026-10-18T03:32Z. All gates pass: solvability 10/10, size 276 tokens, 3/3 variants, the start graph fails at V6 (f2p false, p2p true), and all 17 valid mutants are killed. Under the corrected oracle the reviewer's ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-05/alt05_w1000.grc (2.4/3.6 kHz, width 1000) now passes V6 with purity 0.999005. alt05_w950 passes with 0.999233 and alt05_n2425w950 with 0.999427. Yet authoring_notes.borderline_designs and the build.py docstring still say that this design 'gives 99.883 % (29.3 dB) ... and is rejected'. The docstring's 'rectangular window (96.8 %)' now measures 0.975408 (mutant #14). The three variants all score at least 99.987 %, far from the 99.9 % threshold. alt05_w1000 passes by only 5e-6 (0.02 dB), so if it were added as a variant now, the variants gate would depend on float rounding until the threshold is changed as F2 proposes.
findings.suggested_fix: First decide F2's threshold. Then recompute the numbers in the build.py docstring and authoring_notes under the corrected oracle, and add the reviewer's 2.4/3.6 kHz designs to VARIANTS in build.py: w950 and n2425w950 now, and w1000 once the threshold leaves a margin. Rebuild the item and re-run the gates.

findings.claim: Requirement (1) gives the clock frequency 'within 1 %', but any clock other than exactly 600 Hz fails requirement (3). The cause is real, not FFT leakage. When a period is not a whole number of samples, the aliases of the sampled square wave's high harmonics no longer fall on odd harmonics of the clock, and some of them land in the band-pass. The oracle is therefore right to reject these answers, but the instruction promises a freedom that does not exist. Unlike gbf-test-12, windowing band_fraction would not change this result.
findings.evidence: I ran ./gb ladder on the reference with the clock set to 600.5, 601, 603 and 597 Hz, all within the stated 1 %. Each fails V6 on purity alone: 0.987145, 0.992542, 0.977158 and 0.977297. The probe ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-05/compliance/probe_leak05.py measures the same outputs with a Kaiser window (beta 14), on the same 8000 samples and on 48000 samples. It gives 0.997264, 0.995684, 0.989208 and 0.989244, all below 99.9 %. At exactly 600 Hz the result is 0.999983. The build.py docstring relies on the 80-sample period ('all their spectral lines (aliases included) fall on odd harmonics').
findings.suggested_fix: State that the new clock is exactly 600 Hz, i.e. 80 samples per period at 48 kHz, and remove 'within 1 %' from (1), from (2) for the 3 kHz, and from spec_properties. The 6 Hz and 30 Hz peak_freq tolerances can stay as measurement slack. No oracle change is needed.

findings.claim: The item follows the split rule as written, and its dev assignment was not obtained by signature shopping. But chains that work exactly like this dev item hash to train. The training hand-off also lists 'hand-written chains' as an allowed source without stating the chain-signature rule. Training-side generators may therefore produce functional twins of a dev item that steers prompt and checkpoint choices. This is the set-level issue already raised in gbf-test-04 F1, gbf-test-12 F4 and gbf-dev-06 F2; this finding gives this item's own data.
findings.evidence: compose.signature_split gives 'dev' for the signature of the reference and of the start graph. It stays 'dev' when the clock tap is listed second (the signature becomes analog_sig_source_x|blocks_file_sink) and when the Multiply Const comes before the filter, so the split does not depend on connection order or stage order. Equivalent chains move to train: a Throttle inserted before the filter or before the sink, or fir_filter_xxx with band-pass taps in place of band_pass_filter. A low_pass_filter or high_pass_filter chain moves to test. handoff/training_team/flowgraph_seed_split.md and splits/flowgraph_seed_split.json hold only the seed-file split; neither gives SIGNATURE_SEED, SHARES or the rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide this at set level in fix_plan.json. Partition by a normalised signature: drop inert blocks such as Throttle, map all FIR filter block ids to one class, and ignore the order of linear stages. Hand that rule to the training team, then confirm this item still hashes to dev.
